summary: Bug-fix verification for 'many features cannot be opened'. Verified all 16 sidebar pages for Super Admin, 14 for Guru, 12 for Siswa. Every page rendered its main content with the expected data-testid, and NO 'destroy is not a function' or Emergent Runtime error overlay appeared. 42/42 navigations passed.
critical_code_review_comments: useEffect(() => { load(); }, []) pattern is correct across all 11 refactored pages (arrow body returns undefined, not the Promise) - fix is properly applied and stable under React 19 StrictMode.
Minor: several 401 console errors observed briefly during login redirect race (NotificationBell / initial fetches) - non-blocking but could be silenced by gating fetches on auth-ready state.
test_credentials: Used from /app/memory/test_credentials.md - Super Admin, Guru, Siswa all verified working
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend-only bug-fix verification for React 19 StrictMode crash on 11 pages. All sidebar navigations tested for SA/Guru/Siswa - all render correctly with proper data-testid. Deep flows (QR scan, uploads, candidate creation) were intentionally NOT tested per request. If regression needed, re-run the playwright loop over MENUS_SA/GURU/SISWA arrays and assert data-testid presence + no 'destroy is not a function' text.
rca of the issue: Prior bug: pages used useEffect(load, []) where load returned a Promise; React treated the Promise as a cleanup function, causing 'destroy is not a function' crash on re-mount under StrictMode. Fix: wrap in arrow -> useEffect(() => { load(); }, []) so the effect callback returns undefined. Verified applied on: Schoolgram, Assignments, Quizzes, UangKas, SocialFund, Announcements, MasterAccounts, Attendance, Inventory, Elections, Feedback (Calendar was already fixed).
